subject: Mathematics
source: National Curriculum (KS2 Year 3: place value to 1000; addition and subtraction; 3, 4 and 8 times tables)

lessons.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
objectives: Recognise the place value of each digit in a 3-digit number
Read and write numbers to 1000 in numerals and words

keywords.def: groups of one hundred; the left digit in a 3-digit number
the value a digit has because of its position
one of the symbols 0 to 9

starter: Say Bismillah. Count in 10s from 40 to 120.
How many tens and ones are in 67?

teach.heading: Ten tens make a hundred
teach.note: Use base ten blocks (flat, rod, cube). Ask: how many rods in a flat? The pattern of tenfold exchange is the heart of place value.

teach.heading: Reading 346
teach.note: Build 346 and read it. Ask what each digit is worth. Misconception: reading 346 as 'three, four, six'.

teach.heading: Zero as a placeholder
teach.note: Compare 305 and 35 using blocks. Ask what is different. Pupils often write 'three hundred and five' as 3005.

teach.heading: Words and numerals
teach.note: Practise the word to numeral link and 'and' after hundreds. Show that 1000 is ten hundreds.

practice: What is the value of the 7 in 372?
Write 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones as a number.
independent: Write each as a number: 3 hundreds 2 tens 8 ones; 9 hundreds 0 tens 1 one; 5 hundreds 5 tens.
Write the value of the 6 in 463, the 9 in 295 and the 1 in 810.
Write in numerals: six hundred and forty; two hundred and three; nine hundred and ninety-nine.
exit: What is the value of the 8 in 483?
Write seven hundred and six as a numeral.
lessons.homework: Write five 3-digit numbers, then write each in words and say the value of each digit.
lessons.send: SEND: use base ten blocks and a place value chart. Stretch: write numbers beyond 1000 using thousands.

lessons.title: Partitioning 3-digit numbers
objectives: Partition a 3-digit number into hundreds, tens and ones
Partition in different ways

keywords.def: split a number into parts
a number written as the sum of the values of its digits

starter: Bismillah. What is the value of the 5 in 253?
Write four hundred and nine as a numeral.

teach.heading: Standard partitioning
bullets: Draw it with a part-whole model.
teach.note: Show the model with 538 at the top and three parts. Add the parts to check you get 538.

teach.heading: Numbers with zeros
bullets: Do not write 0 tens in the sum.
teach.note: Ask: what do we do when a digit is zero? We can leave that part out or write + 0.

teach.heading: Flexible partitioning
teach.note: Show that one hundred can be exchanged for ten tens. This prepares for column subtraction.

teach.heading: Missing parts
teach.note: Children find missing hundreds, tens or ones. Ask them to explain how they used place value.

practice: Partition 764 into hundreds, tens and ones.
independent: Write 560 in three different ways.
lessons.homework: Choose four 3-digit numbers and write each in two different partitioned ways.
lessons.send: SEND: use place value counters on a chart. Stretch: partition 4-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Number lines and estimating to 1000
objectives: Identify and estimate numbers on a number line to 1000
Find the number halfway between two numbers

keywords.def: work out an approximate answer or position
the numbers marked along a line or axis

teach.heading: Reading a scale
bullets: Work out what each gap is worth.
teach.note: Always find the scale first: count the number of equal gaps and divide. Show lines with 0-1000, 100-200 and 300-400.

teach.heading: Placing a number
bullets: Nearer the middle, just past halfway.
teach.note: Use 650 as a benchmark. 640 is just before it. Ask: how can you tell?

teach.heading: Halfway numbers
teach.note: Teach halving the gap. Ask pupils to explain how to find the halfway number between 300 and 500.

teach.heading: Missing labels
bullets: On a line from 300 to 400, marks are every 10.
teach.note: Show a segment with unlabelled ticks. Pupils count on in tens from the first label.

practice: What number is halfway between 100 and 200?
On a 0 to 1000 line, is 860 nearer 800 or 900?
independent: Draw a line from 0 to 1000 with marks at every 100. Mark 250, 700 and 910.
An arrow is at 360 on a line from 300 to 400. Mark its position.
Write the halfway number between: 600 and 700; 150 and 250; 0 and 800.
exit: Estimate the position of 480 on a 0 to 1000 line.
lessons.homework: Draw your own number line from 0 to 1000 and mark ten numbers that you choose.
lessons.send: SEND: use pre-drawn lines with fewer marks. Stretch: use number lines with decimals or thousands.

lessons.title: Comparing and ordering 3-digit numbers
objectives: Compare 3-digit numbers using <, > and =
Order numbers from smallest to largest

keywords.def: decide which is larger or smaller
in order from smallest to largest
in order from largest to smallest

teach.heading: Compare hundreds first
teach.note: Lay the numbers one above the other in a place value chart. Start from the left each time.

teach.heading: Same hundreds
teach.note: When a column is equal, move right. Use blocks to show the difference of 14.

teach.heading: Ascending and descending
teach.note: Sort by hundreds then tens. Explain the words ascending and descending.

teach.heading: Between
teach.note: Challenge: find a number between 399 and 401. This tests the crossing of hundreds.

independent: Order largest to smallest: 215, 521, 152, 512, 251.
A number has 4 hundreds. Its tens digit is bigger than its ones digit. Write three possibilities.
lessons.homework: Write eight 3-digit numbers using the digits 2, 5 and 8 (each once) and order them.
lessons.send: SEND: use a place value chart for every comparison. Stretch: compare 4-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Counting in 50s and 100s; 10 and 100 more or less
objectives: Count in multiples of 50 and 100
Find 10 or 100 more or less than a number

keywords.def: a number you get when you count in steps of a given number
add 10; the tens digit goes up by 1

teach.heading: Counting in 100s
teach.note: Chant together. Ask which digit changes when we add 100. The tens and ones stay the same.

teach.heading: Counting in 50s
teach.note: Link to 50p coins: two make a pound. Ask: what is the 8th multiple of 50? (400)

teach.heading: 10 more, 10 less
teach.note: Show the tens digit changing. Highlight the crossing of a hundred. Use a hundred square extended to 1000.

teach.heading: 100 more, 100 less
teach.note: Show the hundreds digit changing. 100 less than 50 can be left for stretch.

independent: Complete: 10 more than 589 is __; 10 less than 700 is __; 100 more than 899 is __; 100 less than 506 is __.
Write a rule for the sequence 120, 220, 320, 420.
lessons.homework: Choose six numbers between 100 and 900 and write 10 more, 10 less, 100 more and 100 less for each.
lessons.send: SEND: use a hundred square and counters. Stretch: count in 25s or 1000 more and less.

lessons.title: Counting in 4s and 8s; number patterns
objectives: Count in multiples of 4 and 8
Spot patterns in sequences

keywords.def: a list of numbers following a rule
the instruction that tells you how to get from one term to the next

teach.heading: Counting in 4s
teach.note: Use doubling: the 4s are the doubles of the 2s. Chant to 12 x 4 = 48.

teach.heading: Counting in 8s
teach.note: Show 4, 8, 12, 16 and 8, 16, 24, 32 side by side. Each 8s number is the double of the 4s number.

teach.heading: Find the rule
teach.note: Pupils find the difference between neighbours. Check the rule works for every pair.

teach.heading: Missing numbers
bullets: Use the rule to fill in.
teach.note: Pupils fill the gaps and explain. Ask for the next three terms.

independent: Write the first six numbers of a sequence that starts at 5 and adds 8 each time.
lessons.homework: Write out the 4 times table and the 8 times table, circling the numbers that appear in both.
lessons.send: SEND: use a multiplication square to highlight. Stretch: count in 6s and 9s.

lessons.title: Place value problems and review
objectives: Solve problems using place value
Make numbers from given digits

keywords.def: a card with one digit used to build a number

teach.heading: Make the number
teach.note: Place the largest digit in the hundreds. Ask: what is the smallest number? (358)

teach.heading: Make all numbers
bullets: With 3, 5 and 8 there are six numbers.
teach.note: Show a systematic listing (fix the hundreds digit). Systematic working prevents repeats.

teach.heading: Clues
bullets: My tens digit is 6. My ones digit is 3 less than my tens.
teach.note: Pupils solve the number riddle step by step. Ask: what is the ones digit? (3)

teach.heading: Explain it
teach.note: Introduce unusual partitions. Ask pupils to prove it with blocks.

practice: Use digits 2, 6 and 9 to make the smallest number.
I am a 3-digit number. My digits add to 6. I am between 300 and 400 and I am even with 0 tens. What am I?
independent: List all six numbers using 1, 4 and 7. Order them.
Make three numbers greater than 700 using 3, 7 and 9.
Write a riddle for the number 582.
exit: Make the largest number with 2, 5 and 9.
lessons.homework: Make up three number riddles and ask someone at home to solve them.
lessons.send: SEND: provide digit cards to move. Stretch: use four digits and thousands.

lessons.title: Mental addition and subtraction with 3-digit numbers
objectives: Add and subtract ones, tens and hundreds mentally
Choose efficient mental strategies

keywords.def: a way to work out an answer in your head
go through a multiple of ten or hundred in steps

starter: Bismillah. Make the largest number from 3, 6, 4.

teach.heading: Ones, tens and hundreds
teach.note: Change only the digit that matches the value. Ask which column changes each time.

teach.heading: Subtract the same way
teach.note: Check using addition. Watch for crossing a ten or hundred, e.g. 503 - 6.

teach.heading: Bridging
teach.note: Make the next ten first. Use a number line. Link to Y2 bridging, now with a hundreds digit.

teach.heading: Near multiples
teach.note: Round to the nearest hundred and adjust. Also try 436 - 98 = 436 - 100 + 2 = 338.

independent: Solve by bridging: 197 + 6, 502 - 5, 438 + 7.
Solve by adjusting: 256 + 98, 623 - 99, 407 + 101.
lessons.homework: Write ten mental calculations from this lesson with their answers and the method used.
lessons.send: SEND: use a number line and base ten. Stretch: mental addition of two 3-digit numbers like 340 + 270.

lessons.title: Column addition without exchange
objectives: Add two 3-digit numbers using the column method
Line up digits correctly

keywords.def: a written method with digits lined up by place value
the result of adding

teach.heading: Line them up
bullets: Tens under tens, ones under ones.
teach.note: Show a place value grid with H, T, O headings. Misalignment is the main error with different-length numbers.

teach.heading: Add from the right
teach.note: Always start with the ones, because any exchange moves left. Here 324 + 251 = 575.

teach.heading: Check by estimating
teach.note: Teach estimation after every calculation. Ask: would 1575 be sensible?

teach.heading: Different lengths
teach.note: Show a 2-digit number aligned correctly. Emphasise filling the empty hundreds with a blank or 0.

independent: A school has 245 girls and 312 boys. How many pupils?
Find the missing digit: 3_4 + 215 = 569.
lessons.homework: Solve six column additions with no exchange and check each with an estimate.
lessons.send: SEND: use squared paper for alignment. Stretch: add three 3-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Column addition with exchange in the ones
objectives: Add 3-digit numbers when the ones total more than 9
Carry a ten to the tens column

keywords.def: swap ten ones for one ten
write the new ten in the next column

teach.heading: Ones make more than 9
teach.note: Use place value counters: exchange ten ones for one ten counter in the tens column.

teach.heading: Add the tens
teach.note: Show the carried 1 written beneath the tens column. Ask pupils to remember to add it.

teach.heading: Add the hundreds
teach.note: Check the reasonableness against the estimate. 384 is close to 390.

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: This one needs exchanges in both ones and tens. Work through it slowly (previewing next lesson): 12 ones, 5+7+1 = 13 tens, 4+2+1=7 hundreds.

independent: Spot the mistake: 243 + 129 = 362.
A shop sold 237 and 184 loaves in two days. How many in total?
lessons.homework: Solve six additions with an exchange in the ones and check each by estimating.
lessons.send: SEND: use counters on a place value mat. Stretch: add 4-digit numbers with exchange.

lessons.title: Column addition with exchange in tens and ones
objectives: Add 3-digit numbers with more than one exchange
Work accurately with zeros

keywords.def: swap 10 of one unit for 1 of the next unit

teach.heading: Two exchanges
teach.note: Use counters on a place value chart to model each exchange. The hundreds then: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8.

teach.heading: Answer and check
teach.note: Always compare with an estimate. Ask: would 8043 or 743 be sensible?

teach.heading: Exchange over 1000
teach.note: Show the thousands exchange as a stretch. Place value chart with a thousands column.

teach.heading: Zeros
teach.note: A tricky case. 407 + 395 = 802: ones 12 so 2 carry 1; tens 0+9+1 = 10 so 0 carry 1; hundreds 4+3+1 = 8.

independent: Two lorries carry 364 kg and 479 kg. What is the total?
Make up an addition where both the ones and tens need exchange.
exit: Estimate first, then check your answer.
lessons.homework: Solve six additions with two exchanges and estimate each answer first.
lessons.send: SEND: use a template with arrows for the carry. Stretch: use 4-digit addition.

lessons.title: Column subtraction without exchange
objectives: Subtract a 3-digit number from a 3-digit number without exchange
Check using addition

keywords.def: taking one amount from another to find what is left
the operation that undoes another

teach.heading: Set it out
bullets: Write the larger number on top.
teach.note: The larger number goes first in subtraction. Show 587 above 342.

teach.heading: Subtract each column
teach.note: 587 - 342 = 245. Ask pupils to say each step aloud. Misconception: subtracting the smaller digit from the larger.

teach.heading: Check with addition
teach.note: Teach the inverse check each time. The answer plus the number subtracted should give the start number.

teach.heading: Zeros in the answer
bullets: Write the 0 to hold the place.
teach.note: Show that a zero in the answer is needed. Do not leave a gap.

independent: A shop has 785 pens and sells 342. How many left?
Find the missing digit: 6_8 - 235 = 433.
lessons.homework: Solve six column subtractions with no exchange and check each by addition.
lessons.send: SEND: colour the columns differently. Stretch: subtract 3-digit numbers from 4-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Column subtraction with exchange
objectives: Subtract 3-digit numbers when exchange is needed
Exchange from the tens or hundreds

keywords.def: swap one ten for ten ones (or one hundred for ten tens)
break one unit into ten of the unit below

teach.heading: Not enough ones
teach.note: Use counters: change a ten counter into ten ones. The tens column becomes 4 and the ones 13.

teach.heading: Complete the sum
teach.note: Check by adding: 325 + 128 = 453. Show the crossing-out layout.

teach.heading: Not enough tens
teach.note: 5 hundreds 3 tens 2 ones becomes 4 hundreds 13 tens 2 ones, then 4 hundreds 12 tens 12 ones. Work slowly.

teach.heading: Finish and check
teach.note: Check with addition. Ask pupils to explain why the hundreds became 4.

independent: A library has 652 books. 378 are borrowed. How many are left?
Spot the mistake: 504 - 227 = 377.
exit: How do you check your answer?
lessons.homework: Solve six subtractions with exchange and check each by addition.
lessons.send: SEND: place value counters on a mat. Stretch: subtractions across zeros, such as 600 - 258.

lessons.title: Estimating and checking calculations
objectives: Estimate answers to addition and subtraction by rounding
Use inverse operations to check

keywords.def: find an approximate answer
change a number to a nearby simpler one
the operation that undoes another

teach.heading: Round to estimate
teach.note: Rounding to the nearest 100 makes the calculation simple. The exact answer is 602.

teach.heading: Is it sensible?
teach.note: Ask pupils to find an unreasonable answer, e.g. 1602. Estimating catches carry errors.

teach.heading: Inverse check
teach.note: Show both checks: estimate for size and inverse for exactness.

teach.heading: Subtraction estimate
teach.note: Rounded 296 to 300 so the estimate is slightly lower than the exact answer. Discuss.

independent: Maryam says 387 + 214 = 701. Use an estimate to decide if she is correct.
Write two calculations whose estimate is 500.
lessons.homework: Write six calculations, estimate each, solve it and check by the inverse.
lessons.send: SEND: use a rounding number line. Stretch: estimating with 4-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Addition and subtraction word problems
objectives: Solve one- and two-step word problems with 3-digit numbers
Choose operations and methods

keywords.def: a problem needing two calculations
a diagram using bars to show the parts and the whole

teach.heading: Understand
bullets: What do we know and want to know?
teach.note: Show a bar divided into parts. Label the known and unknown values.

teach.heading: One-step example
bullets: A shop sells 345 apples and 278 pears.
teach.note: Check using an estimate: 350 + 280 = 630.

teach.heading: Two-step example
teach.note: Break into two steps. Ask what the first calculation tells us before we do the second.

teach.heading: Check the answer
teach.note: Teach a checking routine: answer sentence, estimate, inverse.

practice: A school has 468 pupils. 175 are in KS1. How many are not in KS1?
Ali walked 345 m and 278 m. How far in total?
Ayesha has 600 beads. She uses 255, then buys 130. How many now?
independent: A farmer has 824 eggs. He sells 357 and packs 190. How many are left unsold and unpacked?
A bus journey is 468 km. After 239 km, how far is left?
Make up a two-step problem with the answer 275.
exit: A tank holds 750 litres. 285 litres leaks out. How much is left?
Which operation did you use and why?
lessons.homework: Write and solve three word problems about things you see in your home.
lessons.send: SEND: use a step-by-step template. EAL: pre-teach vocabulary. Stretch: problems with three steps.

lessons.title: Recap: 2, 5 and 10 times tables
objectives: Recall multiplication and division facts for the 2, 5 and 10 times tables
Understand multiplication as equal groups

keywords.def: find the total of equal groups
the answer to a multiplication
objects arranged in equal rows and columns

teach.heading: Equal groups
teach.note: Show repeated addition as multiplication. Draw an array of 3 rows of 5.

teach.heading: Commutative
teach.note: Rotate the array to show 5 rows of 3. This halves the number of facts to learn.

teach.heading: Division is the inverse
teach.note: Link to a fact family: 3, 5 and 15. Ask: what is 15 / 5?

teach.heading: 2s, 5s and 10s facts
teach.note: Quick-fire practice with a times table square. Ask for patterns: ends in 0 or 5 for the 5s.

independent: Fill the table: 2 x 1 to 2 x 12; 5 x 1 to 5 x 12; 10 x 1 to 10 x 12.
A pack has 5 pens. How many pens in 8 packs? How many packs for 35 pens?
lessons.homework: Practise the 2, 5 and 10 times tables for five minutes every day.
lessons.send: SEND: use arrays and a times table square. Stretch: 11 times table.

lessons.title: The 3 times table
objectives: Recall multiplication and division facts for the 3 times table
Use the facts to solve simple problems

keywords.def: a number in the 3 times table
a number that divides exactly into another

teach.heading: Count in 3s
bullets: Use fingers or a number line.
teach.note: Chant to 36. Show jumps on a number line. Notice that the digits of the multiples of 3 add up to a multiple of 3 (for fun).

teach.heading: Build facts
teach.note: Use arrays of 3 rows. Note that 3 x 4 is double 3 x 2.

teach.heading: Division facts
teach.note: Use the multiplication facts backwards: 3 x 9 = 27 so 27 / 3 = 9.

teach.heading: Problem
teach.note: Link to class organisation. Ask pupils to write both the multiplication and the division sentence.

independent: Complete: 3 x 4, 3 x 8, 3 x 6, 3 x 11.
A bag holds 3 oranges. How many bags for 30 oranges? How many oranges in 9 bags?
lessons.homework: Write out the 3 times table and learn it using look, cover, write, check.
lessons.send: SEND: times table grid with highlighted 3s. Stretch: 6 times table as double of 3s.

lessons.title: The 4 times table
objectives: Recall multiplication and division facts for the 4 times table
Use doubling to derive the 4 times table

keywords.def: multiply by 2
a number that divides exactly into another

teach.heading: Double double
teach.note: Doubling twice is multiplying by 4. Use blocks or arrays.

teach.heading: The facts
teach.note: Chant and write them out. Notice the ones digits repeat 4, 8, 2, 6, 0.

teach.heading: Division facts
teach.note: Use the facts backwards. Halve then halve again gives division by 4.

teach.heading: Problem
teach.note: Everyday contexts. Ask pupils to tell the multiplication and division sentences.

independent: Complete: 4 x 5, 4 x 9, 4 x 11, 4 x 12.
A packet of stickers has 4 stickers. How many in 12 packets? How many packets for 36 stickers?
lessons.homework: Learn the 4 times table. Ask someone to test you, then write down the facts you got wrong.
lessons.send: SEND: use multiplication arrays and a times table square. Stretch: 12 x 4 and 40 x 4.

lessons.title: The 8 times table
objectives: Recall multiplication and division facts for the 8 times table
Derive 8s from the 4s by doubling

keywords.def: a number in the 8 times table

teach.heading: Double the 4s
teach.note: Use the relationship. Ask pupils to double the whole 4s row to get the 8s.

teach.heading: The facts
teach.note: Chant to 96. The ones digits go 8, 6, 4, 2, 0 and repeat.

teach.heading: Division
teach.note: Use the facts in reverse. Halve, halve, halve is dividing by 8.

teach.heading: Problem
teach.note: Contexts such as spiders' legs or pizza slices work well. Ask pupils for the inverse sentence.

independent: Complete: 8 x 3, 8 x 7, 8 x 10, 8 x 12.
Eight children each have 8 marbles. How many marbles? 96 marbles shared by 8 children?
lessons.homework: Practise the 3, 4 and 8 times tables with a family member.
lessons.send: SEND: use a times table square with 8s highlighted. Stretch: 16 x 8 using doubling.

lessons.title: Using times tables to solve problems
objectives: Use 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 10 times tables in word problems
Link multiplication and division

keywords.def: the operation that undoes another
the result of multiplying
the result of dividing

teach.heading: Fact families
teach.note: Revisit fact families with multiplication. Ask pupils to write the family for 4, 6 and 24.

teach.heading: Missing numbers
teach.note: Use the inverse. 36 / 4 = 9. 48 = 8 x 6 so the last answer is 48.

teach.heading: Word problems
teach.note: Write the number sentence first, then solve. Check with the inverse.

teach.heading: Two-step problems
bullets: 4 packs of 5 pens. 3 pens are lost.
teach.note: Show how to break the problem into two parts. Ask what to find first.

practice: Write the four facts for 3, 7 and 21.
independent: Complete the fact family for 4, 9, 36.
Find the missing numbers: 5 x __ = 35, __ / 4 = 7, 8 x __ = 72.
A coach seats 40 children. Each minibus seats 8. How many minibuses for the same number? Each table seats 4: how many tables for 40 children?
exit: 6 boxes hold 8 pens each. How many pens?
lessons.homework: Write six word problems using times tables, with answers on a separate sheet.
lessons.send: SEND: bar model templates for each problem. Stretch: 3 times table in a two-step problem with remainder.
